rca of the issue:
User-reported bug RCA: B2B users perceived the Opwaarderen tab inside the Merken wallet as 'B2C-looking' because the tab content was just a plain '

Kies een campagne-pakket

' + a grid of cards — visually identical to a generic shop list, with none of the distinctive 'VOOR MERKEN / Campagne-pakketten' eyebrow + hero treatment that the public landing page (pp-merken-pakketten-v1.js) uses to signal MERKEN context. The user's screenshot showed they wanted the Opwaarderen tab to look exactly like the public landing. Mitigation v60.1.157: (a) replace the bp-section-titel h2 with a full bp-wallet-hero block carrying class pp-b2b-campagne-hero, eyebrow 'Voor merken', h2 'Campagne-pakketten', and the intro paragraph 'Kies het pakket dat past bij je doelen. Saldo wordt gebruikt voor advertenties, placements en boosts binnen Paskamerpraat.'; (b) reuse the existing _renderB2BPackagesHTML() helper so the 4 cards (Starter/Groei-POPULAR/Pro/Ultimate with VERWACHTING blocks) are emitted by the same render path the public landing uses → visual parity by construction; (c) change CTA text on each card from 'Wallet opwaarderen' to 'Opwaarderen' to align with the public landing's CTA voice; (d) preserve the top-level Saldo hero before the tabs so the page hierarchy is Saldo → tabs → Opwaarderen-with-Campagne-hero (two heroes total); (e) bump cache-key on pp-wallet-v1.js to v60.1.157-merken-campagne-layout and sw.js VERSION to v60.1.157-20260623-merken-campagne-layout so end users get the new file on next service-worker activation. PP_Wallet.topup() intercept + source:'b2b' chain untouched → popup still wins. B2C wallet untouched → zero cross-contamination. Public landing untouched → no regression on logged-out marketing surface. Verification: 66 pytest assertions all green, ZIP MD5 matches, /api/downloads returns the updated zip.
